html:
Nanzhao was a kingdom centered on Yunnan, in today's southwest China, from 738 to 902. Its capital stood near Lake Erhai, at modern Dali. The map shows it from 800 to 1200, so the label also covers the Dali Kingdom that followed.

Piluoge united six small principalities in 738 with Tang support. His successor turned against the Tang, allied with the Tibetan Empire, and destroyed Tang armies in 751 and 754. Nanzhao switched back to the Tang side in 794. It was a strong military state that raided in every direction: it raided Chengdu in Sichuan in 829, sacked the capital of the Pyu in Burma in 832, and attacked Annam in the 860s. Its rulers were Buddhist and drew on Chinese, Tibetan and Indian culture.

A minister seized the throne in 902. After some unstable decades, Duan Siping founded the Dali Kingdom in 937 on the same land. Dali lasted until 1253, when a Mongol army under Kublai Khan conquered it on the way to outflank the Song. Yunnan has been ruled from China ever since.
